trust_decision.summary: Caller-supplied per-part name, filename and content_type are trusted as header-safe and interpolated raw into multipart part headers in Req.Utils.encode_form_part/2; no escaping or CR/LF/quote check exists anywhere on the path.

landing_point.why: The summary names multipart name/filename/content_type; the only multipart encoder is encode_form_part in Req.Utils, which the :form_multipart option in encode_body calls directly (lib/req/steps.ex:495). An engineer lands on the header-building lines 575-590 at once.

fix_sites.entry_point: Req.request/post with form_multipart field name (atom or string key) -> Req.Steps.encode_body/1; fix also adds is_atom(name) guards at lib/req/utils.ex:537 and :597 (fix.diff:76, fix.diff:107)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: Single multipart implementation in the pinned tree: lib/req/utils.ex:503-599 is the only code emitting part headers (only @crlf/content-disposition hits in lib/). No second implementation, wrapper or lower-level API.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Weak: a solver could argue that string-keyed field names (map input / [{"k", v}] list), which reach lib/req/utils.ex:589 the same way as atom keys, are undocumented (docs at lib/req/steps.ex:416-432 just say name/value pairs, and the examples use keyword lists). But a name-escaping fix covers both key types, so the argument fails in practice.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate content_type values with parameters (e.g. "text/plain; charset=utf-8"), filenames with spaces, non-ASCII or ';', and the default filename/content_type derived from a File.Stream path must still go through unchanged. The fix percent-encodes only '"', CR and LF (fix.diff:112-114), so an over-broad URI.encode, quoting or rejection breaks them. Existing tests check the exact bytes and content-length (test/req/steps_test.exs:273, :280-281).

O6_input_shapes: field name: atom key (escaped via Atom.to_string, fix.diff:98)
field name: string key (map or tuple-list input) - rejected by the new is_atom guard rather than escaped (fix.diff:76, fix.diff:107)
bare value vs {value, options} tuple (two encode_form_part clauses, lib/req/utils.ex:537, :597)
filename defaulted from File.Stream path via Path.basename (lib/req/utils.ex:550, :562) - covered because escaping happens after the default
explicit :content_type option, and content_type defaulted via MIME.from_path (lib/req/utils.ex:563-565)

O7_producer.where: The defaults for filename/content_type are filled inside the same function (lib/req/utils.ex:560-565) before the sink; there is no separate schema/serializer/config producer.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Reachable custom :boundary option: e.g. a request option form_multipart_boundary forwarded from lib/req/steps.ex:495 and interpolated unchecked into every part delimiter and the content-type header (lib/req/utils.ex:510, :519, :590).
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: encode_form_multipart already accepts :boundary (line 504) and tests use it (test/req/utils_test.exs:236). Exposing it as a step option for servers that need a fixed boundary is a plausible feature, and its value then lands in both the body and a request header.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: An extra per-part option such as :headers (a list of extra part headers, e.g. content-transfer-encoding) appended next to content-type at line 584.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Keyword.validate! already whitelists per-part options, and extra part headers are a common feature request for multipart encoders. That would add a how-type sibling where the header name, not just the value, needs validating.

O9_family: CRLF / header injection (CWE-93) in a multipart/form-data body encoder

O10_build.toolchain: Elixir ~> 1.15 / Erlang OTP, mix (deps: finch, mime, jason; test deps plug, bandit, bypass, aws_signature, castore)
O10_build.project_tests: test/req/utils_test.exs:200-330 (describe encode_form_multipart, exact byte-level body assertions, no network); test/req/steps_test.exs:268-318 (form_multipart through a plug: adapter, offline)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Escape or reject only the field name (the most visible interpolation, lib/req/utils.ex:589) or only CR/LF, leaving '"' in filename or content_type, or validate only user-passed options in encode_body and miss the Path.basename default.

out_of_scope_notes: Req.Utils.encode_form_multipart/2 :boundary option (lib/req/utils.ex:504-510) goes unchecked into delimiters and content-type, but encode_body never passes it (lib/req/steps.ex:495) and Req.Utils is @moduledoc false (lib/req/utils.ex:2); not part of the advisory's per-part property.
General request-header CR/LF validation (put_header etc.) is left to the adapters (Finch/Mint); not examined.
